name: MARC II Pipeline
monitor_reason: concrete step: only a non-binding open season in October 2014 is documented (indications above 700 MMcf/d); no FERC filing, permit application, precedent agreement, EPC award or FID found, and the project later lapsed. Length (about 30 mi, about 48 km) would pass the 25 km rule. Cancellation is not independently sourced.
researcher_notes: No existing GEM row under this or another name (roster has no MARC I or MARC II row; the 2012 MARC I Hub Line is a separate completed project, EIA historical sheet row 735). A World Pipelines article of 21 October 2014 states Crestwood Midstream, through Central New York Oil and Gas, concluded a non-binding open season for a proposed new 30 mile pipeline from its system to the proposed PennEast Pipeline, a new Transco Leidy Line interconnect and Transco's proposed Atlantic Sunrise Expansion in Luzerne County, Pennsylvania. The article gives no diameter. The 30-inch size and the cancelled status in the queue note were not verified. The EIA projects workbooks in the repo contain no MARC II entry. If a FERC pre-filing or a second independent source for the cancellation is found, revisit as a new row of 30 mi (cancelled, Owner Central New York Oil & Gas Company LLC, parent Crestwood Midstream Partners LP, ProposalYear 2014). Single source, low tier.
